author: certara-jcraig
body:
To support cases where simulated data is not a replicate of the observed data. [#64]
- Add optional `repl` argument in `simulated.tidyvpcobj` to identify replicate column in simulated data
- Add `data.sim` argument in `stratify.tidyvpcobj` to identify strata in simulated data
- Change existing non-replicate error checks to warnings
- Both `binning()` and `binless()` are supported

Example usage:

``` r
library(data.table)
library(tidyvpc)
library(magrittr)

# Can additionally toggle tidyvpc package specific verbosity
options("tidyvpc.verbose" = TRUE)

obs <- tidyvpc::obs_data[MDV==0]
sim <- tidyvpc::sim_data[MDV==0]
sim$GENDER <- rep(obs$GENDER, nrow(sim) / nrow(obs))

sim_rich <- sim[, {
  ntime_seq <- seq(from = min(TIME),
                   to   = max(TIME),
                   by   = 0.01)
  dv_interp <- approx(x = TIME, y = DV, xout = ntime_seq)$y
    data.table(TIME = ntime_seq,
             DV    = dv_interp,
             GENDER = GENDER[1])
}, by = .(ID, REP)]


vpc <- observed(obs, x = TIME, yobs = DV) %>%
  simulated(sim,
            ysim = DV) %>%
  binning(bin = "jenks", nbins = 5) %>%
  vpcstats()

plot(vpc)

vpc_non_rep <-
  observed(obs, x = TIME, yobs = DV) %>%
  simulated(sim_rich,
            xsim = TIME,
            ysim = DV,
            repl = REP) %>%
  binning(bin = "jenks", nbins = 5) %>%
  vpcstats()

plot(vpc_non_rep)

vpc_non_rep_strat <-
  observed(obs, x = TIME, yobs = DV) %>%
  simulated(sim_rich,
            xsim = TIME,
            ysim = DV,
            repl = REP) %>%
  stratify(~ GENDER, data.sim = sim_rich) %>% #specify data.sim arg 
  binning(bin = "jenks", nbins = 5) %>%
  vpcstats()

plot(vpc_non_rep_strat)
```

author: madcampos
body:
## Summary

Main features:

- Update the route definitions to generate openapi docs and to use zod schemas for validation.
- Update database schema to align more with designs
- Add some standardized APi responses
  - [HATEOAS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HATEOAS) responses using [HAL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypertext_Application_Language)
  - Status response consisting only of message and an optional error
  - Paginated response with fields needed to build pagination

## Tests

<!-- Tell us if the changes have been tested and how -->
None 🫠

## Additional information

### Database schemas

- Add command to run migrations on the database using wrangler. (This creates all tables on a local db).
- Add sql migration scripts with all of the fields documented.
- Add sample seed script with very minimal data for testing. (This can definitely be improved!)
- Make schemas/types for data cascade in a way that helps to keep them in sync[^1].

### Standardized responses

- Add HATEOAS so the response can be used to link to other urls using a very simple schema. This basically means adding a `_links` object with some links to related things to the response.
- Add a status response that is used throughout for anything that represents a status message and does not contain any "data". The meaning of the response, like if it is an error or a success should be inferred by the http status code[^2].
- Add the skeleton for a pagination type of response, as well as `TODO` comments to actually implement pagination. (This PR is already doing a lot as it is... 🫠🙃)

### Openapi docs

- The format for writing endpoints has changed to use the `app.openapi` format instead of `app.<http method>`.
- `app.openapi` requires a call to `createRoute` to document the api route. This is strictly typed and have lots of type sorcery going on, so typescript will actually yell if things are not conforming to the types. That means some changes:
  - Using `res.json({} satisfies Type)` instead of `res.json<Type>()`. For some reasons beyond my feeble mind one works, the other don't. The end results are the same for us.
  - Changing `StatusCodes` to be a [`const const`](https://www.totaltypescript.com/concepts/as-const) instead of an `enum`. The usage is the same, but it behaves _slightly_ differently... [^3]
  - _EVERYTHING_ has to be a zod schema, both responses and request parameters. The good part is the openapi addition does validation for us; the bad part is that we can't write simple `type ...` or `interface ...` anymore, it _has to go through_ zod... 🫠

### Miscellaneous
- Shout out to @pmjuu by catching that we need to validate if an id exists on the db before updating or deleting it! I've made that validator a little more generic and applied it throughout the CRUD routes.
- I've added a check so a request the tries to create a profile with an existing email will error out.
- A couple eslint rules are relaxed so they are warns instead of errors or will not error out

[^1]: The schemas move as follows: main entity > create > update (E.g.: Team > Create Team > Update Team). So all properties exist for results when retrieving data, creation allows to add everything, and update makes most fields optional. There is an extra restriction to not change the id, schema version or insertion timestamps.

[^2]: Sending a 200 response with `{ isError: true }` is a sin and people who write this type of abomination should suffer by writing Java and XML servers for the rest of eternity! __*BE WARNED!*__

[^3]: While the `const` with the `as const` annotation is a plain js object that will suffer no conversion, an `enum` suffers some transformations by the typescript compiler. Some people prefer to avoid enums because they are both types (that can be removed) and actual code, so they are in a weird spot between ts and js. Here is a more in depth read about enums: https://2ality.com/2025/01/typescript-enum-patterns.html

author: lobsterkatie
body:
Currently, if an event has a hybrid fingerprint (a fingerprint including both `{{ default }}` and a custom value), we don't send it to Seer, because we don't want to override the custom grouping the user has chosen to do. That said, the whole point of hybrid fingerprints (as opposed to fully custom ones) is that the user wants grouping to happen as normal before their custom grouping is applied. If using Seer is now part of "normal grouping," it follows that it should be included in the preliminary step when grouping events with hybrid fingerprints. This PR makes that change (albeit behind a new `organizations:grouping-hybrid-fingerprint-seer-usage` feature flag).

The key insight here was provided by @JoshFerge: Rather than trying to insert a Seer call into the middle of the process of combining default grouping values with custom ones to get an initial hash value, we can achieve the same effect by considering the custom values twice: once when calculating the hash, and again when evaluating the Seer result. With the hash, we're matching on the two pieces (normal grouping, custom fingerprint) combined into a single value. With Seer, we can match on the two pieces individually, and the totality of the result is the same. In concrete terms, this means that for events with hybrid fingerprints, the Seer result only "counts" if the custom pieces match as well.

Note: In order to compare the two fingerprints, we rely on the resolved fingerprint value stored in grouphash metadata. (For the incoming event, it's important to use its grouphash and not the fingerprint in the event itself, because in the event, fingerprint variables like `{{ message }}` and `{{ transaction }}` appear in their raw, unevaluated form. That fingerprint _is_ enough to determine hybrid-ness, though, so we use it for that to avoid having to make an extra database request.) This reliance on metadata means this feature will only be as good as the data that backs it up, and will therefore produce limited results until we backfill metadata for all hashes.

### **Summary of Changes:**
This pull request implements an efficient solution for finding duplicates in a list of integers using a dictionary, adding the nested loop approach. The new approach reduces the time complexity from O(n²) to O(n). In addition, it also adds answers to the README file in the lab03-exercises directory.

### **What was added:**

- Implemented find_duplicates_using_dict function in find_duplicates.py
- Added tests for several sample inputs
- Added answers to problem in README file in the lab03-exercises directory

### **Changes in Detail:**

- The New Approach (Dictionary-based):
- A dictionary (hashmap) is used to track the frequency of each element.
- When an element appears more than once, it's added to the duplicates list.
- An element is added to the duplicate list only after the first occurrence.

### **Dictionary Method**
def find_duplicates_dict(l: list) -> list:

    freq_map = {}
    duplicates = []

    for i in l:
        if i in freq_map:
            if freq_map[i] == 1:
                duplicates.append(i)
            freq_map[i] += 1
        else:
            freq_map[i] = 1

    return duplicates
